critique: The implementation of the one final validator-repair opportunity introduced by P2-V0.23.23 is a fresh model-generation request rather than a possible replay of an earlier validator-rejected cached prediction. The IMPLEMENT request attempted Luna, Terra, and Sol under the existing admitted-agent order. Luna returned a proposal rejected by protected validation after about 66.4 seconds, Terra returned a proposal rejected by protected validation after about 35.8 seconds, and Sol reached the 60-second hosted-model timeout. The final repair correctly selected the most recent validator-rejected admitted agent, Terra, but the repair request contained the same Work Specification, source context, and static `VALIDATOR_REPAIR_GUIDANCE` unchanged. The final-repair-only constraint includes a bounded deterministic context token derived solely from server-owned run revision, work-unit identity, assignment generation, and the token exists to make request identity cache-distinct and observable; it grants no authority and contains no source text, rejected output, provider payload, credential, environment value, or filesystem path.
